Converting to a polyline is often required before exporting to CNC post-processors and older systems that cannot read NURBS; PELLIPSE does the same for ellipses at creation time. A spline with a tolerance greater than zero does not pass exactly through its fit points.

tools.name: HATCHEDIT
tools.description: Change an existing hatch or gradient fill: pattern, scale, angle, colour, transparency, origin, layer and draw order, and its relationship to the boundary. Boundaries can be added, removed or recreated, and a single hatch covering several areas can be separated into independent hatches. The leading-hyphen version -HATCHEDIT does the same from the command line, which is what scripts need.
tools.usage:
HATCHEDIT  (alias HE; command-line version -HATCHEDIT)
Select hatch object: <object>
(opens the Hatch Edit dialog)

-HATCHEDIT
Select hatch object:
Enter hatch option [DIsassociate/Style/Properties/DRaw order/ADd boundaries/
Remove boundaries/recreate Boundary/ASsociate/separate Hatches/Origin/ANnotative/LAyer/Transparency]:

parameters.name: Properties (P)
parameters.description: Change the pattern name, scale and angle - the options needed by nearly every scripted edit.

parameters.name: ADd boundaries / Remove boundaries
parameters.description: Extend the hatch into another area or exclude an island without redrawing the hatch.

parameters.name: recreate Boundary (B)
parameters.description: Draw a new polyline or region around the hatch, and optionally associate the hatch with it - the rescue for a hatch whose boundary was deleted.

parameters.name: ASsociate / DIsassociate
parameters.description: Link the hatch to its boundary so it follows edits, or break that link permanently.

parameters.name: separate Hatches (H)
parameters.description: Split one hatch object that fills several separate areas into one hatch per area.

parameters.name: Origin (O)
parameters.description: Move the point the pattern is aligned from, which is what makes brick, block and tile patterns start in the right place.

parameters.name: DRaw order (DR)
parameters.description: Send the hatch behind or in front of other objects without a separate DRAWORDER command.

parameters.name: HPASSOC / HPORIGIN / HPLAYER
parameters.description: System variables for the associativity, origin and layer defaults applied to new hatches.

tools.example:
; Rescale every ANSI31 hatch in the drawing
(setq ss (ssget "_X" '((0 . "HATCH"))))
(setq i 0)
(repeat (sslength ss)
  (command "_-HATCHEDIT" (ssname ss i) "_P" "ANSI31" 50 0)
  (setq i (1+ i)))

; Recreate a lost boundary and re-associate
-HATCHEDIT
(select the hatch)
B
P
Y
tools.notes: Always use -HATCHEDIT in scripts and macros; the plain command opens a dialog that a script cannot drive. A hatch whose boundary was erased shows as non-associative and cannot follow edits until recreate Boundary is used. HATCHTOBACK sends every hatch in the drawing behind everything else in one command, which is usually what a busy drawing needs.

tools.name: TEXTEDIT
tools.description: Edit the contents of an existing annotation object: single-line text, mtext, dimension text, multileader text and attribute definitions. The Mode option decides whether the command ends after one object or keeps asking for the next, which makes correcting a run of labels quick. Double-clicking the object runs the same command.
tools.usage:
TEXTEDIT  (alias ED; replaces the older DDEDIT)
Current settings: Editing mode = Multiple
Select an annotation object or [Undo/Mode]: <object> | U | M
(Mode) Enter a text editing mode [Single/Multiple] <Multiple>:
(TEXT objects edit in place; MTEXT opens the in-place editor)

parameters.name: Mode (M)
parameters.description: Single ends the command after one object, Multiple keeps prompting for the next until Enter.

parameters.name: Undo (U)
parameters.description: Reverse the last edit without leaving the command.

parameters.name: objects accepted
parameters.description: TEXT, MTEXT, dimension text, multileader text and attribute definitions (ATTDEF). Attribute values in an inserted block are edited with EATTEDIT instead.

parameters.name: MTEXTED
parameters.description: System variable naming the editor used for mtext; the default in-place editor cannot be driven by a script.

parameters.name: FIND
parameters.description: The command to use for bulk text changes: it searches and replaces across the drawing, including block attributes and dimension overrides.

tools.example:
; Correct two labels in one run
TEXTEDIT
M
(pick the first text)
ROOM 12
(pick the second text)
ROOM 13


; AutoLISP: change every TEXT string on a layer, no dialog
(setq ss (ssget "_X" '((0 . "TEXT") (8 . "NOTES"))))
(setq i 0)
(repeat (sslength ss)
  (setq e (entget (ssname ss i)))
  (entmod (subst (cons 1 "ISSUED FOR CONSTRUCTION") (assoc 1 e) e))
  (setq i (1+ i)))
tools.notes: Scripts should not use TEXTEDIT for mtext because the in-place editor blocks them; change the DXF group 1 value with entmod, or use FIND for a search and replace. TEXTEDIT changes only the string - height, style and justification are changed in the Properties palette or with CHANGE. TXT2MTXT converts several single-line texts into one mtext object.

tools.name: EATTEDIT
tools.description: Edit the attributes of one inserted block through the Enhanced Attribute Editor, which shows each attribute's value on one tab, its text formatting on another, and its layer, colour, linetype and lineweight on a third. It changes that single block reference only, leaving the definition and all other insertions untouched. Double-clicking a block that has attributes opens it.
tools.usage:
EATTEDIT
Select a block: <block reference>
(dialog) Attribute | Text Options | Properties

; Command-line alternative for scripts
-ATTEDIT
Edit attributes one at a time? [Yes/No] <Y>: N
Enter block name specification <*>: / Enter attribute tag specification <*>:
Enter attribute value specification <*>:
Enter string to change: / Enter new string:

parameters.name: Attribute tab
parameters.description: Lists every attribute tag, its prompt and its value; edit the value here.

parameters.name: Text Options tab
parameters.description: Text style, justification, height, rotation, width factor, oblique angle and backwards or upside-down flags for the selected attribute.

parameters.name: Properties tab
parameters.description: Layer, linetype, colour, lineweight and plot style of the attribute text.

parameters.name: -ATTEDIT
parameters.description: The command-line attribute editor. Answering No to 'one at a time' gives a global find-and-replace across attribute values filtered by block name, tag and value - the only practical scripted way to change many attributes.

parameters.name: ATTDISP
parameters.description: System command controlling global attribute visibility: Normal, ON (show even invisible ones) or OFF.

tools.example:
; Change every TAG_NO value from P-000 to P-101 across the drawing
-ATTEDIT
N
*
TAG_NO
P-000
ALL

P-000
P-101

; AutoLISP: read and write an attribute directly
(setq att (entget (entnext (car (entsel)))))
(entmod (subst (cons 1 "P-101") (assoc 1 att) att))
tools.notes: EATTEDIT affects one insertion; BATTMAN changes the definition for all of them and ATTSYNC pushes those changes out. Attribute changes made here are per-insertion overrides and are lost if ATTSYNC is later run against the block. ATTIPE and ATTMULTI control the in-place attribute editor and multiline attributes.

tools.name: BATTMAN
tools.description: Manage the attribute definitions belonging to a block: reorder the prompts, edit a definition's mode, text settings and properties, remove an attribute altogether, and push the changes out to every existing insertion. It is the tool for maintaining title blocks and equipment tags once they are already in use, because the alternative - redefining the block by hand - loses attribute values.
tools.usage:
BATTMAN
(dialog) Block: <name> / attribute list
Buttons: Sync | Move Up | Move Down | Edit... | Remove | Settings...
Edit dialog tabs: Attribute | Text Options | Properties

parameters.name: Sync
parameters.description: Apply the current definition to all existing insertions of the block, the same operation as ATTSYNC.

parameters.name: Move Up / Move Down
parameters.description: Change the order attributes are prompted for at insertion and listed in extraction.

parameters.name: Edit
parameters.description: Change a definition's tag, prompt, default, modes (invisible, constant, verify, preset, lock position, multiple lines) and its text and property settings.

parameters.name: Remove
parameters.description: Delete an attribute from the definition; it disappears from every insertion when the block is synchronised.

parameters.name: Settings
parameters.description: Choose which columns the list shows and whether changes are applied to existing references automatically.

parameters.name: Auto preview / Apply changes to existing references
parameters.description: Controls whether insertions update immediately or wait for a synchronisation.

tools.example:
; Typical sequence when a title block gains a new field
BEDIT
TITLEBLOCK_A1
ATTDEF
(define the new attribute)
BSAVE
BCLOSE
BATTMAN
(select the block, reorder the prompts, press Sync)

; Or synchronise from the command line
ATTSYNC
N
TITLEBLOCK_A1
tools.notes: Synchronising resets per-insertion overrides such as a moved or restyled attribute, so warn users before running it on a drawing where attributes have been repositioned. Values of attributes that still exist are preserved; new attributes take their default value and removed ones are deleted. ATTREDEF is the older command that redefines a block and its attributes in one step and is far more destructive.

tools.name: ATTSYNC
tools.description: Update every insertion of a block so it matches the current attribute definitions in the block definition. Attributes that still exist keep their values, newly added attributes appear with their default value, and attributes that were deleted from the definition are removed from the insertions. Run it after editing a block's attributes in the Block Editor or with BATTMAN.
tools.usage:
ATTSYNC
Enter an option [?/Name/Select] <Select>: ? | N | S
(?) lists the blocks in the drawing
(Name) Enter block name: <name>
(Select) Select a block: <block reference>
ATTSYNC block <name>? [Yes/No] <Yes>:

parameters.name: Name (N)
parameters.description: Synchronise by block name, which is what scripts use because no picking is involved. Wildcards are accepted.

parameters.name: Select (S)
parameters.description: Pick an insertion in the drawing and synchronise that block definition.
List the block definitions in the drawing before choosing one.

parameters.name: value preservation
parameters.description: Existing values are kept for tags that still exist; new tags get their default, deleted tags are removed.

parameters.name: property overrides
parameters.description: Position, text style, height and other per-insertion attribute overrides are reset to the definition.

tools.example:
; Synchronise a single block by name
ATTSYNC
N
EQUIP_TAG
Y

; Synchronise everything matching a prefix
ATTSYNC
N
TB_*
Y
tools.notes: This is the command that undoes careful manual repositioning of attributes, so check with the drawing's author first. It does not change attribute values - use -ATTEDIT or a LISP routine for that. BATTMAN's Sync button runs the same operation on the block being managed.

tools.name: BEDIT
tools.description: Open a block definition in the Block Editor, where its geometry, attributes and dynamic behaviour are edited and saved back to the drawing. Every insertion of the block updates when the definition is saved. It is also the only place where dynamic block parameters and actions - stretch, flip, array, visibility states, lookup tables - can be created.
tools.usage:
BEDIT  (alias BE; command-line version -BEDIT)
(dialog) Block to create or edit: <name> | <Current Drawing>

-BEDIT
Enter block name or [?]: <name>

; Inside the editor
BPARAMETER / BACTION / BACTIONTOOL / BVSTATE / BCONSTRUCTION / BSAVE / BCLOSE

parameters.name: block name
parameters.description: The definition to open; choosing <Current Drawing> edits the drawing itself as a block, which is how the drawing's own base geometry gains dynamic behaviour.

parameters.name: BSAVE / BSAVEAS
parameters.description: Save the definition back into the drawing, updating every insertion, or save it under a new name.

parameters.name: BCLOSE
parameters.description: Leave the Block Editor, prompting to save if there are unsaved changes.

parameters.name: BPARAMETER / BACTION
parameters.description: Add dynamic block parameters (point, linear, polar, rotation, flip, alignment, visibility, lookup, base point) and the actions driven by them.

parameters.name: BVSTATE
parameters.description: Create and manage visibility states so one block can show several variants.

parameters.name: BLOCKEDITLOCK
parameters.description: System variable that locks the Block Editor so standard blocks cannot be altered by users.

parameters.name: BCONSTRUCTION
parameters.description: Turn geometry into construction geometry that is visible only inside the editor.

tools.example:
; Open a block, add a hidden attribute, save and close
-BEDIT
VALVE_GATE
-ATTDEF
I

MANUF
Manufacturer:

0,0
2.5
0
BSAVE
BCLOSE

; Then update existing insertions
ATTSYNC
N
VALVE_GATE
Y
tools.notes: Saving in the Block Editor updates every insertion immediately and cannot be undone selectively. -BEDIT is the form to use in scripts so no dialog appears. REFEDIT edits a single reference in place in the drawing context instead, which suits small corrections; BEDIT is right when the definition itself is wrong.

tools.name: REFEDIT
tools.description: Edit an external reference or a block reference in place, in the context of the current drawing, so the surrounding geometry can be seen and snapped to. Selected objects form a working set that can be changed, added to and removed from, and the result is saved back to the source block definition or xref file. It is the right tool for a small correction that needs the surrounding drawing for reference.
tools.usage:
REFEDIT
Select reference: <xref or block reference>
(dialog) Identify Reference | Settings

; Companion commands used inside the edit session
REFSET   Transfer objects to or from the working set [Add/Remove]
REFCLOSE Save back changes or Discard reference changes

parameters.name: working set
parameters.description: The objects opened for editing. Objects not in the set are dimmed by the XFADECTL setting and cannot be modified.

parameters.name: REFSET
parameters.description: Add objects from the drawing into the reference, or remove objects from the reference into the drawing.

parameters.name: REFCLOSE
parameters.description: Save the changes back to the xref file or the block definition, or discard them.

parameters.name: XEDIT
parameters.description: System variable in the source drawing that decides whether it may be edited in place when referenced by others; set it to 0 to protect standard details.

parameters.name: Nesting level
parameters.description: The dialog lets you pick how deep into nested references the edit applies - Automatically select all nested objects, or prompt to select them.

parameters.name: XFADECTL
parameters.description: How strongly objects outside the working set are faded during an in-place edit.

tools.example:
; Correct a symbol inside a block, in place
REFEDIT
(select the block reference)
(accept the dialog)
ERASE
(pick the wrong line)

LINE
(draw the replacement)

REFCLOSE
S

; Pull a stray object into the reference first
REFSET
A
(select the object)
tools.notes: Saving changes to an xref writes to the source DWG file, which affects every drawing that references it - make sure that is intended and that you have write access. Attributes and objects on locked or frozen layers behave unpredictably in a reference edit; unlock first. BEDIT is the better choice for substantial block work, and XOPEN opens an xref in its own window for major changes.

tools.name: MATCHPROP
tools.description: Copy properties from one source object to any number of destination objects. By default it copies colour, layer, linetype, linetype scale, lineweight, transparency, thickness and plot style, plus the object-specific properties of dimensions, text, hatches, polylines, viewports, tables, materials and multileaders. The Settings option opens a checklist so only the wanted properties are transferred.
tools.usage:
MATCHPROP  (alias MA; also PAINTER)
Select source object: <object>
Current active settings: Color Layer Ltype Ltscale Lineweight Transparency
Thickness PlotStyle Dim Text Hatch Polyline Viewport Table Material Multileader
Select destination object(s) or [Settings]: <objects> | S

parameters.name: Settings (S)
parameters.description: Open the Property Settings dialog and tick exactly which basic and special properties are copied - the option that turns MATCHPROP from blunt to precise.

parameters.name: Basic properties
parameters.description: Colour, layer, linetype, linetype scale, lineweight, transparency, thickness and plot style.

parameters.name: Dimension / Text / Hatch
parameters.description: Special properties that copy the whole style: dimension style, text style, and hatch pattern, scale and angle.

parameters.name: Polyline
parameters.description: Copies width and linetype generation, but not the geometry itself.

parameters.name: Viewport
parameters.description: Copies the on/off state, display locking, standard or custom scale, shade plot and snap/grid settings between layout viewports.

parameters.name: Multileader / Table / Material
parameters.description: Copies multileader style, table style and the assigned material.

tools.example:
; Make a set of hatches match an existing one, pattern and all
MATCHPROP
(select the good hatch)
(select the hatches to fix)


; Copy only the layer, nothing else
MATCHPROP
(select the source)
S
(untick everything except Layer, OK)
(select the destinations)
tools.notes: The settings persist for the session, so a MATCHPROP that unexpectedly changes a text style is usually the result of an earlier Settings change. Properties set BYLAYER are copied as BYLAYER, so the destination picks up the source's layer behaviour rather than fixed values. SETBYLAYER is the companion that resets explicit colours, linetypes and lineweights back to BYLAYER across a selection.

tools.name: PROPERTIES
tools.description: Open the Properties palette, the central place where the properties of the current selection are read and changed: layer, colour, linetype, geometry values such as radius and length, text contents and style, and every object-specific setting. With nothing selected it shows and sets the current defaults for new objects. It is a palette, so scripts use CHPROP or CHANGE instead.
tools.usage:
PROPERTIES  (aliases PR, CH, MO; Ctrl+1)
PROPERTIESCLOSE  closes the palette

; Command-line equivalents, usable in scripts
CHPROP
Select objects:
Enter property to change [Color/LAyer/LType/ltScale/LWeight/Thickness/TRansparency/Material/Annotative]:

CHANGE
Specify change point or [Properties]:

parameters.name: CHPROP
parameters.description: Change colour, layer, linetype, linetype scale, lineweight, thickness, transparency, material or the annotative flag of a selection without any dialog.

parameters.name: CHANGE
parameters.description: Does what CHPROP does and also edits the defining points of lines, circles, text and attribute definitions - the old but still useful way to restyle text from a script.

parameters.name: QUICKPROPERTIES / QPMODE
parameters.description: The small floating properties panel that appears on selection, and the system variable that turns it on or off.

parameters.name: PICKADD
parameters.description: Whether new picks add to the selection (1) or replace it (0); it is exposed as the small toggle at the top of the palette and confuses people when it is off.

parameters.name: current defaults
parameters.description: With no selection the palette sets CECOLOR, CELTYPE, CELWEIGHT, CELTSCALE and the current layer for new objects.

tools.example:
; Script-safe: move a selection to a layer and set it BYLAYER
CHPROP
ALL

LA
EQUIPMENT

C
BYLAYER


; Change the height of every text object on a layer
CHANGE
(select the text)

P
(properties option)

; From AutoLISP, directly
(setq e (entget ent))
(entmod (subst (cons 8 "EQUIPMENT") (assoc 8 e) e))
tools.notes: The Properties palette cannot be driven by a script or a menu macro; always reach for CHPROP, CHANGE, SETBYLAYER or entmod in automation. Values shown as *VARIES* mean the selection is mixed - typing a value there applies it to everything selected. Ctrl+1 toggles the palette, and PROPERTIESCLOSE closes it from a command.

tools.name: OVERKILL
tools.description: Find and remove duplicate and overlapping geometry: objects drawn exactly on top of each other, collinear lines that partly overlap or meet end to end, and redundant polyline vertices. It is the standard cleanup on drawings received from other offices, converted from other formats, or produced by repeated copying. A tolerance and a list of properties to ignore control how aggressive it is.
tools.usage:
OVERKILL
Select objects: <selection>
(dialog) Delete Duplicate Objects
  Tolerance / Ignore object property: Color, Layer, Linetype, Linetype scale,
  Lineweight, Thickness, Transparency, Plot style, Material
  Options: Optimize segments within polylines, Ignore polyline segment widths,
  Do not break polylines, Combine co-linear objects that partially overlap,
  Combine co-linear objects when aligned end to end, Maintain associative objects

; Command-line version for scripts
-OVERKILL

parameters.name: Tolerance
parameters.description: How close two objects must be to count as duplicates. 0 means an exact match; small non-zero values catch rounding differences from imported files.

parameters.name: Ignore object property
parameters.description: Tick a property to treat objects that differ only in that property as duplicates - ticking Layer, for example, removes a line that was copied onto another layer.

parameters.name: Optimize segments within polylines
parameters.description: Remove duplicate vertices and straighten redundant segments inside polylines.

parameters.name: Combine co-linear objects that partially overlap
parameters.description: Merge two overlapping collinear lines into one.

parameters.name: Combine co-linear objects when aligned end to end
parameters.description: Merge collinear lines that meet at a point into a single line, which is the same result as JOIN.

parameters.name: Do not break polylines
parameters.description: Leave polylines intact even when parts of them duplicate other geometry.

parameters.name: Maintain associative objects
parameters.description: Protect associative hatches, dimensions and arrays from being broken by the cleanup.

tools.example:
; Clean a whole imported drawing
OVERKILL
ALL

(set Tolerance 0.000001, tick the combine options, OK)

; Command-line form for an unattended script
-OVERKILL
ALL

Done
tools.notes: Run OVERKILL on a copy first and compare the object count before and after; ignoring Layer or Color can delete geometry that was deliberately duplicated. It does not remove objects that merely look identical at the current zoom, only genuine geometric duplicates within the tolerance. PURGE, AUDIT and -PURGE clean the symbol tables rather than the geometry, and are the other half of a drawing cleanup.

tools.name: REVERSE
tools.description: Reverse the direction of lines, polylines, splines and helixes, so the object runs from its old end point to its old start point. Direction matters more than it seems: linetypes containing text or asymmetric shapes read backwards along a reversed object, path arrays and sweeps run the wrong way, and annotation attached to a direction follows suit. The geometry itself does not move.
tools.usage:
REVERSE
Select objects to reverse direction: <selection>
Select objects: Enter

parameters.name: objects accepted
parameters.description: Lines, 2D and 3D polylines, splines, helixes and elliptical arcs - anything with a start and an end.

parameters.name: effect on linetypes
parameters.description: Linetypes carrying text or shapes, such as a gas or fence line, are drawn along the object's direction and read correctly only one way round.

parameters.name: PEDIT Reverse
parameters.description: The same operation from inside PEDIT for a polyline.

parameters.name: SPLINEDIT Reverse
parameters.description: The same operation from inside SPLINEDIT for a spline.

tools.example:
; Flip every polyline on a layer so the linetype text reads correctly
(setq ss (ssget "_X" '((0 . "LWPOLYLINE") (8 . "SERVICES"))))
(command "_REVERSE" ss "")

; Single object
REVERSE
(select the polyline)
tools.notes: Reversing changes only the vertex order, so nothing visibly moves except direction-dependent linetypes and the behaviour of path arrays, sweeps and lofts. Check the result by turning on the polyline direction arrows in the Properties palette or by regenerating. An associative path array attached to a reversed curve redistributes its items along the new direction.

tools.name: DRAWORDER
tools.description: Control which objects are drawn on top when geometry overlaps: send objects to the front or the back, or place them directly above or below a chosen object. It is essential wherever solid hatches, wipeouts, images and filled areas would otherwise hide text and linework. Draw order affects both the screen and the plot.
tools.usage:
DRAWORDER  (alias DR)
Select objects: <selection>
Enter object ordering option [Above object/Under object/Front/Back] <Back>: A | U | F | B
(Above/Under) Select reference object:

parameters.name: Front (F) / Back (B)
parameters.description: Move the selection in front of or behind everything else in the drawing.

parameters.name: Above object (A) / Under object (U)
parameters.description: Position the selection immediately in front of or behind one named reference object.

parameters.name: TEXTTOFRONT
parameters.description: Companion command that brings all text, dimensions, leaders or all three to the front in one operation - the usual fix for text hidden by a hatch.

parameters.name: HATCHTOBACK
parameters.description: Companion command that sends every hatch in the drawing behind all other objects.

parameters.name: DRAWORDERCTL
parameters.description: System variable controlling whether draw order is maintained automatically during editing, traded off against performance on large drawings.

tools.example:
; Push a wipeout behind the note it supports
DRAWORDER
L

B

; Put a symbol directly above a hatch
DRAWORDER
(select the symbol)

A
(select the hatch)

; Standard end-of-drawing cleanup
HATCHTOBACK
TEXTTOFRONT
A
tools.notes: Draw order is stored per space, so objects in model space and in a layout are ordered independently. Objects inside a block share the block's position in the order; changing the order of one component means editing the block. If the plotted result differs from the screen, check DRAWORDERCTL and regenerate before blaming the plotter.

tools.name: GROUP
tools.description: Collect objects into a named or unnamed group that is selected and moved as one unit, without the permanence of a block. Groups keep the objects independent - they stay on their own layers and can still be edited individually - which makes them the right tool for a temporary or loose association such as a furniture arrangement or a set of related annotations. PICKSTYLE and Ctrl+Shift+A decide whether picking one member selects the whole group.
tools.usage:
GROUP  (alias G; command-line version -GROUP; the old dialog is CLASSICGROUP)
Select objects or [Name/Description]: <selection> | N | D

UNGROUP  (alias UNG)      dissolve a group
GROUPEDIT                 [Add objects/Remove objects/REName]

-GROUP
Enter a group option [?/Order/Add/Remove/Explode/REName/Selectable/Create] <Create>:

parameters.name: Name (N)
parameters.description: Give the group a name so it can be referred to later; unnamed groups are created with an internal *An name.

parameters.name: Description (D)
parameters.description: A text description stored with the group.

parameters.name: GROUPEDIT
parameters.description: Add objects to or remove objects from an existing group, or rename it.

parameters.name: UNGROUP
parameters.description: Dissolve the group, leaving the objects in place and unchanged.

parameters.name: PICKSTYLE
parameters.description: 0 no group or associative hatch selection, 1 group selection, 2 associative hatch selection, 3 both. Ctrl+Shift+A toggles group selection.

parameters.name: -GROUP Selectable
parameters.description: Turn an individual group's selectability on or off, so one group can be edited member by member while others stay locked together.

parameters.name: -GROUP Explode
parameters.description: The command-line equivalent of UNGROUP.

tools.example:
; Create a named group from a selection
GROUP
(select the objects)

N
WORKSTATION_01

; Add an object later
GROUPEDIT
(select the group)
A
(select the object)


; Temporarily edit members individually
PICKSTYLE 0
(edit a single member)
PICKSTYLE 1
tools.notes: Groups are a selection convenience, not a definition: unlike a block, changing one group does not change another, and there is no reuse. An object can belong to more than one group, which quickly becomes confusing. When members must stay identical across many places, use a block with BEDIT instead. CLASSICGROUP reopens the pre-2012 Object Grouping dialog for anyone who prefers it.
